root_causes.description: The cart pod (cart-69bd7c567b-5ccmp) was killed and restarted during the incident window — it is the only pod in the namespace with a restart (counter increase max=1.108) and its container shows Created/Started count=2. The restart caused cart server p99 latency to spike to ~52ms (vs ~2ms baseline, ~25x), propagating upstream to frontend and checkout (p99 ~48ms each), which triggered the high-latency-p99 watchdog.

evidence.observed_value: cart-69bd7c567b-5ccmp restarts max=1.108 during window; all other pods = 0.000

evidence.query_or_id: Created: Container created (count=2); Started: Container started (count=2); Pulled: Container image "ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.0.0-cart" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod (count=1)
evidence.observed_value: cart container recreated/restarted twice (Created count=2, Started count=2); no OOMKilled or BackOff events observed
evidence.expected_baseline: single container creation, no restart events

evidence.observed_value: cart p99=51.703ms, max=53.660ms, anomaly detected at 1789645720.696; frontend p99=48.485ms; checkout p99=48.000ms
evidence.expected_baseline: cart p99 ~1.98ms (consistent with other leaf services: currency, payment, shipping, quote all p99=1.980ms)

evidence.observed_value: order-consumed trace involving cart, duration 34379ms, status ok (no errors)

root_causes.description: Alternative hypothesis: cart itself experienced intrinsic high latency (the only service flagged with a latency anomaly in the sweep), e.g. slow storage/serialization, which may have caused health-check failures leading to the container restart. Error rates were ~0 across all services, ruling out http_abort.

evidence.observed_value: cart p99=51.703ms with anomaly flagged; all other leaf services (currency, payment, shipping, quote) p99=1.980ms
evidence.expected_baseline: cart p99 ~2ms consistent with other leaf services

evidence.observed_value: cart error_rate=0.000; max across all services 0.019 (flagd only)
evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01 — no error spike, ruling out http_abort

evidence.observed_value: cart request_rate mean=0.650, max=0.781 — traffic remained present, no total outage

root_causes.description: Cart memory working set rose from ~82MB to ~104MB (+27%) and CPU rose to 0.072 cores (~4x its p50, highest in the cluster) during the window, indicating resource pressure that could have contributed to the container restart; however no OOMKilled event was observed, so this is a secondary contributor at best.

evidence.observed_value: cart-69bd7c567b-5ccmp max=104415232 bytes (~104MB) vs p50=82157568 bytes (~82MB)
evidence.expected_baseline: stable working set ~82MB (flat for all other pods)

evidence.observed_value: cart-69bd7c567b-5ccmp max=0.072 cores vs p50=0.017; all other pods <= 0.013
evidence.expected_baseline: cart CPU ~0.017 cores, in line with other services

remediation_steps: Determine the cart container termination reason: kubectl describe pod cart-69bd7c567b-5ccmp -n otel-demo and inspect lastState/exit code to distinguish an external kill from OOM or liveness-probe failure.
Scale cart to at least 2 replicas with pod anti-affinity so a single pod restart does not remove all cart capacity and spike p99 for frontend and checkout.
Add/tune readiness probes and preStop connection draining on cart so in-flight and queued requests are not stalled during restarts.
Set explicit CPU/memory requests and limits for cart (memory rose ~27% to ~104MB) and consider an HPA to absorb load spikes.
Add retry-with-backoff and circuit breaking in frontend and checkout for cart calls to bound p99 latency during pod churn.
Verify flagd feature-flag/chaos-injection configuration to rule out an intentional cart fault being toggled on during the window.
